topic: Market: worldwide essential tremor prevalence and its rise with age (meta-analysis)

citation: Logemann JA, Fisher HB, Boshes B, Blonsky ER. Frequency and cooccurrence of vocal tract dysfunctions in the speech of a large sample of Parkinson patients. J Speech Hear Disord. 1978;43:47-57; Ho AK, Iansek R, Marigliani C, Bradshaw JL, Gates S. Speech impairment in a large sample of patients with Parkinson's disease. Behav Neurol. 1998;11(3):131-137; Skodda S, Gronheit W, Mancinelli N, Schlegel U. Progression of voice and speech impairment in the course of Parkinson's disease: a longitudinal study. Parkinsons Dis. 2013;2013:389195.
task_or_setup: Expert listener ratings of conversational speech and reading (Logemann, Ho); perceptual and acoustic analysis at two visits (Skodda)
key_quantitative_findings: Logemann: all five co-occurrence groups included laryngeal (voice) dysfunction: 45 % + 13.5 % + 17 % + 5.5 % + 9 % = 90 % of 200 patients (sum is a CALCULATION on the abstract's group shares). Ho: voice was the leading deficit, most frequently affected and impaired in the initial stages; articulation matched voice only at the 'severe' stage. Skodda: voice and speech abnormalities already present in mildly affected patients and worsened over a mean 32.5 months while global motor impairment was largely stable.
limitations: Old perceptual ratings; clinic samples; abstracts only; severity distribution not extracted
relevance_to_design: Dictation is not universally available to people with PD; voice problems are common and progressive
transferability_reason: Perceptual ratings do not map directly to speech-recognition accuracy (see PDT-104)
design_implication: Include dictation as a comparator and record speech intelligibility; do not assume dictation fails for everyone with PD

citation: Wills Act 1837 s.9 (as amended), legislation.gov.uk; Law Commission. Wills project page and final report 'Modernising Wills Law', 16 May 2025; GOV.UK. Make a lasting power of attorney; GOV.UK. Apply for a postal vote.
task_or_setup: Legal and administrative signing requirements
key_quantitative_findings: Wills: valid only if 'in writing, and signed by the testator, or by some other person in his presence and by his direction', made or acknowledged before two or more witnesses present at the same time; video witnessing was allowed only for wills made 31 January 2020 to 31 January 2024. topic: Alternatives: speech input versus touchscreen keyboard speed (typical speakers)
citation: Ruan S, Wobbrock JO, Liou K, Ng A, Landay JA. Comparing speech and keyboard text entry for short messages in two languages on touchscreen phones. Proc ACM Interact Mob Wearable Ubiquitous Technol. 2018.
task_or_setup: Short-message transcription on an iPhone 6 Plus: a research speech recogniser versus the built-in iOS keyboard
participants_or_bench: Typical adult speakers (n not in abstract)
key_quantitative_findings: English: speech 153 vs keyboard 52 words per minute (2.93 times faster); Mandarin 123 vs 43 WPM; corrected error rate 5.30 % vs 11.22 %; uncorrected errors left 1.30 % vs 0.79 %.
units_and_conditions: Words per minute; error rates; laboratory 'upper-bound' conditions
limitations: Healthy participants; laboratory; older recogniser
relevance_to_design: For people whose speech is recognised well, dictation is far faster than any handwriting (compare HAP-159)
transferability_reason: Not people with tremor or PD speech
design_implication: Do not compete on speed of text entry; compete on paper-bound tasks and on people for whom dictation fails

topic: Alternatives: tablet touch accessibility for tremor, built-in dictation, and tablet and stylus prices
citation: Apple. iPad User Guide: 'Adjust how iPad responds to your touch' and 'Dictate text on iPad' (iPadOS); Apple Store US and UK iPad and Apple Pencil pages.
task_or_setup: Accessibility settings and retail prices
key_quantitative_findings: 'If you have difficulties with hand tremors, dexterity, or fine motor control, you can adjust how the iPad touchscreen responds to tap, swipe, and touch-and-hold gestures': Hold Duration, Ignore Repeat, Tap Assistance (initial or final touch location). Dictation: 'you can dictate text anywhere you can type it'; 'processed on your device in many languages, and no internet connection is required'. Prices on 2026-09-30: iPad from USD 449 (US) and GBP 429 (UK); Apple Pencil (USB-C) USD 79; Apple Pencil Pro USD 129.
limitations: No evidence that these settings improve writing or typing in tremor; prices change
relevance_to_design: The digital alternative is free for people who own a device; a tablet app with stylus needs a USD 449-plus tablet
transferability_reason: Mainstream products the target users already own
design_implication: Configure these settings (not defaults) for the typing and dictation conditions of EXP-U06/U07 and time the setup

key_quantitative_findings: Livescribe: Echo 2 USD 119.95; LivePen A5 bundle USD 79.99. design_implication: A subscription near USD 10-50/month is a plausible model for an app; capture alone is not a differentiator

topic: Discovery method: interviews needed for saturation
citation: Hennink M, Kaiser BN. Sample sizes for saturation in qualitative research: a systematic review of empirical tests. Soc Sci Med. 2022;292:114523.
task_or_setup: Review of empirical and modelling studies of saturation
key_quantitative_findings: Studies using empirical data reached saturation within 9-17 interviews or 4-8 focus groups, particularly with relatively homogeneous populations and narrowly defined objectives; multi-country or meta-theme studies needed more.
limitations: Code saturation, not meaning saturation; homogeneous samples
relevance_to_design: Interview numbers per stratum in EXP-U02-U04
transferability_reason: Method evidence
design_implication: Plan 12-16 interviews per homogeneous group (ET, PD, clinicians, parents/teachers) and stop on a pre-set saturation rule

topic: Study method: choosing a pilot size to estimate the SD for the main study
citation: Whitehead AL, Julious SA, Cooper CL, Campbell MJ. Estimating the sample size for a pilot randomised trial to minimise the overall trial sample size for the external pilot and main trial for a continuous outcome variable. Stat Methods Med Res. 2016;25:1057-1073.
task_or_setup: Optimising pilot plus main-trial sample size
key_quantitative_findings: Pilots estimate the SD imprecisely; for a main trial with 90 % power and two-sided 5 % significance, recommended pilot sizes per arm are 75, 25, 15 and 10 for standardised effects of <= 0.1, 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8.
limitations: Parallel-group framing; our designs are within-participant
relevance_to_design: Pilot size for EXP-U06 and the inflation of its SD for EXP-U07
transferability_reason: Parallel-arm guidance applied to paired designs
design_implication: Pilot EXP-U06 with 12-16 participants and plan EXP-U07 with the pilot SD's upper 80 % confidence limit
